How to choose a drawing tablet for beginners

As a starting artist, it is important to know the things to consider when buying a beginner's tablet for drawing.

‍‍That’s why in this article, I also included a buying guide for drawing tablets for beginners.

  1. Price
  2. Pressure Sensitivity
  3. Display
  4. Stylus
  5. Size
  6. Connectivity

And for you to further understand why these factors need to be checked first, here’s a more detailed explanation:

Price

If it is your first time purchasing a drawing tablet, it is not advisable for you to spend too much on it.

Fortunately, there are different brands that are offering a great beginner tablet at an affordable price, like the HUION H610 Pro V2.

However, for starter creatives that really want to invest in a tablet that can make them experience drawing like a pro, the Wacom PTH660 is ideal for you.

At the end of the day, it is important to consider your budget first before buying a drawing tablet, so you won’t regret it in the long run.

Pressure Sensitivity

The most important thing about a drawing tablet is how sensitive it is to the pressure you put on it.

Having more pressure sensitivity means that you can better control the weight of the lines you write.

A drawing tablet with at least 2,048 levels is considered high in pressure sensitivity.

Since you’re still in the process of learning and finding your best drawing style, it is much better to look for a drawing tablet that suits your needs as a beginner.

Display

The screen size and its resolution are other essential thing to consider when buying a tablet for drawing.

Of course, it is better to have a wider screen so that you have a lot of space to draw on.

And with regards to the drawing tablet with a screen, it is best to have a tablet with a high resolution.

In that way, you'll have the best view of your creative work, and you’ll be able to see your drawing in the most accurate way.

Stylus

One of the most important aspects of a drawing tablet is the stylus since it is the one you will use to draw.‍

It should be light and easy to hold, as well as quick and responsive—note that the faster the response time, the less lag you'll see as you draw.

Additionally, there are drawing tablets with pens that don’t have batteries, meaning you can use them no matter how long you want.

These kinds of drawing tablets are ideal for beginning creatives who don’t want to be bothered because their pens run out of power.

Size

Consider how you'll use the drawing tablet while selecting the ideal one for your needs.

Are you seeking a device that is small and portable? Or do you want to work from your desk and prefer a larger screen?

As a beginner, you'll need to balance the benefits and drawbacks of a large or tiny screen.

Larger tablets are heavier and more unwieldy, but they provide a greater area for creation.‍

However, a smaller tablet may easily fit into any suitcase, allowing you to work from anywhere.‍

When it comes to the size of the tablet that you will purchase, it is really a matter of personal preference.

Connectivity

When buying drawing tablets for beginners, you should figure out how to connect the tablet to your PC.

The best tablets include Bluetooth connectivity, which eliminates the need for tangled cords.

You'll also have greater freedom of movement because you won't have to sit directly next to your laptop to work.

However, many tablets still require a USB cable to connect to your laptop, and some require up to three separate wires, which can make your desk look cluttered.

If you like a more structured workstation, check for a Bluetooth-enabled tablet or get one with a 3-in-1 cable to reduce the number of cords on your desk.
